concepts.title: Provider response guarantees
concepts.mechanism: Required Transfer response fields form a promise to clients; removing one from required can break consumer assumptions.

concepts.title: Schema drift versus payload drift
concepts.mechanism: Changing amount type in the declared schema and sending a number while the old schema still requires a string are distinct regressions.

concepts.title: Additive fields and strict consumers
concepts.mechanism: An optional memo works with the open Transfer schema; a strict client may independently reject unknown fields.

misconceptions: Removing a provider response required flag can break older consumers.
A schema type change differs from a response instance type violation.
An optional field can break strict clients despite additionalProperties true.

practice: Mutate schema and JSON payload separately.

segments.objective: Detect removed required response guarantees against an older provider contract.
segments.whyItMatters: An older client can rely on currency being present even when a new schema makes it optional.
segments.mentalModel: Response compatibility flows from provider guarantees toward existing clients.
segments.explanation: Removing currency from required weakens the old provider guarantee. A new response missing currency may fail an older consumer despite the new schema validating it.

segments.objective: Detect breaking type changes and malformed response instances independently.
segments.whyItMatters: A numeric JSON amount can break existing clients expecting a decimal string.
segments.mentalModel: Schema diff catches changed promises while instance validation catches nonconforming emitted data.
segments.explanation: Transfer.amount is a string. Changing the declared type to number breaks the contract; sending a numeric value under the original schema violates it. Missing currency and invalid EUR must also fail.

segments.objective: Test optional field additions with both tolerant and strict legacy consumers.
segments.whyItMatters: A green schema diff is not a guarantee every deployed client accepts unknown properties.
segments.mentalModel: Optional additive evolution is conditional on the actual consumer's unknown-field handling.
segments.explanation: Transfer has additionalProperties true. Adding optional memo preserves the eight required fields and passes a tolerant old schema. A deliberately strict legacy consumer rejects memo, proving consumer review remains necessary.

steps.reason: A green schema diff is not a guarantee every deployed client accepts unknown properties.
steps.expectedResult: Tolerant response passes while strict consumer rejects unknown memo.

reviewQuestions.prompt: Provider menghapus currency dari Transfer.required. Apa risikonya?
options: Tidak berisiko karena schema lebih permisif
Consumer lama dapat menerima response tanpa currency dan gagal
reviewQuestions.explanation: Menghapus required melemahkan janji provider yang mungkin dipakai client lama.

reviewQuestions.prompt: Transfer.amount adalah string tetapi server mengirim number. Apa hasil tes?
reviewQuestions.explanation: Representasi JSON number berbeda dari decimal string pada kontrak.

reviewQuestions.prompt: Field memo baru opsional pada Transfer dengan additionalProperties true. Apa verdict?
reviewQuestions.explanation: Schema open menerima field tambahan, tetapi consumer strict masih harus diuji.

reviewQuestions.prompt: Mengapa schema diff dan payload assertion perlu terpisah?
options: Payload actual dapat salah meskipun schema tidak berubah
reviewQuestions.explanation: Schema drift membandingkan janji dan instance check menilai respons terobservasi.

reviewQuestions.prompt: Legacy consumer memakai reject-unknown-property. Apa yang terjadi jika memo ditambahkan?
options: Dapat gagal walaupun memo opsional dan schema mengizinkan
reviewQuestions.explanation: Kompatibilitas membutuhkan verifikasi consumer aktual, bukan hanya spec check.
